Samantha — thanks for the redlines and the clear list. Quick read-through and proposed approach below so we can shorten the loop: 

1) SOC 2 frequency and bridge letter
- Redwood provides an annual SOC 2 Type II report. If a report period lapses we can provide a SOC 2 bridge letter that covers the gap (high-level controls summary).
- For operational evidence requests, we can support a two-week turnaround for high-risk controls and a monthly cadence for recurring evidence requests. If HealthBridge requires compact monthly windows for particular assertions we can map those to our evidence queue and prioritize by control tags.

2) Pen test / inspection window
- We typically run an annual vendor-managed pen test; customers may run a customer-managed test in a staged environment under an "inspection-lite" clause that limits scope and retains Redwood oversight.
- Proposed default: vendor pen test + optional customer test in staging with a 30-day notice and an agreed 3-business-day staging access window.

3) Access and masking
- Staging access will be ephemeral and read-only where possible; we require redaction/masking of customer PII and any production data.

Next steps/action items: 
- Karthik: can you review and suggest minimal redline language for the inspection-lite clause and the evidence cadence mapping?
- Laura: can you confirm ops feasibility for a prioritized monthly compact window and whether we can commit to 2-week turnarounds for high-risk items on a recurring basis?

If we agree on those three bullets I can prepare a short assurance playbook (1–2 pages) and attach it to the order form. Happy to jump on a 30-min call if you prefer.

— Mina
Head of Assurance Programs | Redwood Inference

Thanks Mina and Samantha — quick legal take and suggested language below. Kept wording narrow to preserve our operations SLAs and avoid broad inspection rights.

Suggested redline bullets for Security Exhibit (to be inserted as short numbered clauses):
1) SOC 2 and Bridge Letter — Redwood will provide Customer with Redwood's annual SOC 2 Type II report within 30 days of request. If Redwood's most recent SOC 2 report does not cover the full term requested, Redwood will provide a SOC 2 bridge letter summarizing controls coverage for the gap period.

2) Penetration Testing — Redwood will perform an annual vendor-managed penetration test against Redwood production and staging per Redwood's internal scope. Customer may perform one customer-managed penetration test per 12-month period against a designated staging environment subject to the following conditions: (a) Customer provides at least 30 days' written notice; (b) Redwood-approved test plan submitted at least 10 business days before the test; (c) Redwood personnel may observe test activities; (d) scope limited to test accounts and non-production data; (e) Customer must not exfiltrate or attempt to access other tenants; (f) Redwood reserves the right to suspend access for safety.

3) Evidence Cadence and Inspection-Lite — Redwood will support prioritized evidence requests via a weekly triage with operational turnarounds as follows: 
- High-risk control evidence: target 10 business days.
- Medium/low-risk control evidence: target 20 business days.
Customer may request compact monthly windows for specified assertions; Redwood will accommodate by designating a prioritized evidence window provided requests are submitted at least 7 business days in advance.

4) Data Masking and Access Controls — Any access granted to staging must respect Redwood's data protection controls. Customer is required to redact or avoid production data and comply with Redwood's data handling checklist for test access.

Comments: I tightened the timelines (10/20 business days) compared to the 2-week/month that Mina suggested to keep expectations conservative. If Mina/Laura confirm ops can reliably meet 10/20 days I can relax these to match the ops proposal.

If Samantha/Bruce are good with the limited inspection model above we can add the clauses to the order form and attach an "Assurance Playbook" that codifies the evidence request flow.

— Karthik
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
